description: Sabotages for windows-overlapped-io-sys's PageBuffers, which holds its pages in an io_buffers::AlignedBuf (IB-2+.2). Run with tools/run-sabotage.ps1; see tools/README-sabotage.md for the format.
notCoveredHere: Only PageBuffers (the fs feature) has entries: this manifest was added with that type's move onto AlignedBuf. The completion-port and operation machinery is not covered.

sabotages.name: IB-2+.2: the pages are allocated at byte alignment
sabotages.why: Page alignment is what the scatter and gather calls require of every segment. The alignment tests read it back from the buffer's own address for several page counts.

sabotages.name: IB-2+.2: each segment starts eight bytes after the last, not a page
sabotages.why: Every segment must name its own page; overlapping segments would read or write the same bytes twice.

sabotages.name: IB-2+.2: the segment array has no terminator
sabotages.why: The kernel reads segments until it meets a zeroed element, so a missing one runs it off the end of the array.

sabotages.name: IB-2+.2: the length is half a page short
sabotages.why: A short length transfers fewer bytes than the buffer holds.

sabotages.name: NR-3: zero pages is not refused
sabotages.why: A buffer with no pages has nothing for a scatter or gather call to name; the constructor refuses it as invalid input, at the caller's own call site.

sabotages.name: NR-3: a page count whose length overflows wraps instead of being refused
sabotages.why: A wrapped length is a small, valid allocation for a count that asked for far more: the buffer would be short of its own page count.

sabotages.name: NR-3: an allocation the machine cannot supply is reported as invalid input
sabotages.why: The count is the caller's and a failed allocation is out of memory, which a caller answers by asking for fewer pages; invalid input would read as a bug in the count's shape.

sabotages.name: NR-3: a page size that is not a power of two is refused by the build
sabotages.why: AlignedBuf refuses such an alignment and `PageBuffers::new` reports every refusal of the allocation as out of memory, so a bad constant would read as out of memory on every call. It is asserted where it is defined.

sabotages.name: IB-2+.2: CONTROL: the page count is read through an identity addition
sabotages.why: Behaviour is unchanged, so a sweep that reports this caught is not discriminating.
